# Updating and proving your pre-settled or settled status

## Summary

You don’t automatically have the right to claim benefits. You must show you have a ‘right to reside’. You might have a right to reside for different reasons - for example, because of things like your work or your family. Check if you have the right to reside. When you go for your interview at the Jobcentre you’ll need to prove your pre-settled status and your right to reside. You can prove you have pre-settled status by either: * printing a copy of your pre-settled status decision letter * giving the Jobcentre a share code so they can view your pre-settled status online - you can get a share code on GOV.UK You'll also need to give the Jobcentre evidence that you have a right to reside. If you’re working, your evidence could be your payslips and contract of employment. If the Jobcentre say they can’t verify your pre-settled status, talk to an adviser. The DWP might ask for proof of your pre-settled status or settled status by adding a message to the journal section of your online account. You should check your journal regularly to make sure you don’t miss any messages. You can give the DWP your share code as evidence - you can get a share code on GOV.UK. If the DWP ask for proof of.

- giving the Jobcentre a share code so they can view your pre-settled status online - you can get a share code on GOV.UK
- you renew or replace the identity document you used to apply - for example, if your passport expires

## Key Information

- Details factual findings that led to the refusal
- Explains whether you have a right of appeal, right to administrative review, or neither
- Specifies the deadline for submitting any appeal or review application
- Submit a fresh application \- appropriate when you can easily address the reasons for refusal (e.g., by providing additional documents), when time is of the essence, when there is no right of appeal or administrative review. - Request for reconsideration \- appropriate where refusal was based on a clear factual error and/or new compelling evidence becomes available post-decision and there is no formal right of appeal or review. # Your options if you're in the UK illegally

## Summary

There are ways to make your stay legal. An immigration specialist will decide which applies to you. Don't worry, getting advice will be confidential - they won't tell anybody about your query. Talk to an adviser for help finding an immigration specialist in your area. You can also call the Joint Council for the Welfare of Immigrants for help. They provide free and confidential advice to people living in the UK illegally. Joint Council for the Welfare of Immigrants Monday, Tuesday and Thursday, 10am to midday Calls to the Joint Council for the Welfare of Immigrants are free. Whether you can live in the UK legally will depend on your circumstances. Your application will probably be refused if you apply more than 14 days after your permission to stay has expired. If you’re not sure when your leave expires, check your biometric residence permit, online immigration status or passport. You might be able to apply to stay in the UK if: * it would be very difficult for you to live in the country you would be in - for example because of a lack of work, education, family or friends, or if you wouldn't be accepted back there * you’ve lived in the UK for 20 years or more * you're aged 18 to 25.

## Key Information

- it would be very difficult for you to live in the country you would be in - for example because of a lack of work, education, family or friends, or if you wouldn't be accepted back there
- you’ve lived in the UK for 20 years or more
- you're aged 18 to 25 and you've lived in the UK for at least half your life
- you can’t return to the country because you’d be persecuted or seriously harmed - for example, if you’d be tortured
- you’ve got a partner who has a right to stay in the UK - for example, if your partner is British or has settled status
- you’ve got children in the UK, especially if they're British citizens, settled or have been in the UK for 7 years or more
- your last visa was as a partner and you've suffered domestic abuse at the hands of the partner related to your visa
- up to 9 months before your sentence ends
- when your sentence has ended
- pay for your medical costs
- There are ways to make your stay legal. An immigration specialist will decide which applies to you. Don't worry, getting advice will be confidential - they won't tell anybody about your query. Talk to an adviser for help finding an immigration specialist in your area.
- You can also call the Joint Council for the Welfare of Immigrants for help. They provide free and confidential advice to people living in the UK illegally.

## Practical Guidance

1. There are ways to make your stay legal. An immigration specialist will decide which applies to you. Don't worry, getting advice will be confidential - they won't tell anybody about your query. Talk to an adviser for help finding an immigration specialist in your area.
2. You can also call the Joint Council for the Welfare of Immigrants for help. They provide free and confidential advice to people living in the UK illegally.
3. Calls to the Joint Council for the Welfare of Immigrants are free.
4. it would be very difficult for you to live in the country you would be in - for example because of a lack of work, education, family or friends, or if you wouldn't be accepted back there
5. you’ve lived in the UK for 20 years or more
6. you're aged 18 to 25 and you've lived in the UK for at least half your life
7. you can’t return to the country because you’d be persecuted or seriously harmed - for example, if you’d be tortured
8. you’ve got a partner who has a right to stay in the UK - for example, if your partner is British or has settled status
9. you’ve got children in the UK, especially if they're British citizens, settled or have been in the UK for 7 years or more
10. your last visa was as a partner and you've suffered domestic abuse at the hands of the partner related to your visa
11. Whether you can live in the UK legally will depend on your circumstances. Your application will probably be refused if you apply more than 14 days after your permission to stay has expired. If you’re not sure when your leave expires, check your biometric residence permit, online immigration status or passport.
12. If you’ve got children living in the UK illegally, it’s important to get advice on whether you can make an application for them. They’ll be living illegally if they haven’t been registered for British citizenship or leave to remain. You can read more about what you can do if your child is here illegally.
- Source: [Your options if you're in the UK illegally](https://www.citizensadvice.org.uk/immigration/deportation-and-living-in-the-uk-illegally/your-options-if-youre-in-the-uk-illegally/)

# Free Legal Advice in England and Wales

## Summary

The November 2025 **Guide to Pro Bono and Other Free Advice in England & Wales** (Attorney General’s Pro Bono Committee) maps government-funded legal aid, pro bono schemes, national advice networks, and specialist charities. It covers England and Wales together; for devolved Welsh law see [[Free Legal Advice in Wales]].

## Key Information

### Overview of help sources (in typical order of consideration)

1. **Online guidance** — [advicelocal.uk](https://advicelocal.uk), [advicenow.org.uk](https://advicenow.org.uk), [citizensadvice.org.uk](https://www.citizensadvice.org.uk); litigants in person: [advicenow.org.uk/get-help/going-court](https://advicenow.org.uk/get-help/going-court), [judiciary.uk guidance](https://www.judiciary.uk/guidance-and-resources/advice-for-litigants-in-person).
2. **Insurance / union / subscription** — some policies and trade unions include legal assistance.
3. **Private lawyers** — [solicitors.lawsociety.org.uk](https://solicitors.lawsociety.org.uk); public access barristers: [directaccessportal.co.uk](https://directaccessportal.co.uk); overview: [legalchoices.org.uk](https://www.legalchoices.org.uk).
4. **Legal aid** — see below.
5. **Housing Loss Prevention Advice Service** — [[Housing Loss Prevention Advice Service]] (not means-tested for qualifying renters/mortgage holders).
6. **Local advice agencies** — Citizens Advice, law centres ([lawcentres.org.uk](https://lawcentres.org.uk)); find via [advicelocal.uk](https://advicelocal.uk), [advicefinder.turn2us.org.uk](https://advicefinder.turn2us.org.uk).
7. **Specialist charities** — by issue (benefits, domestic abuse, immigration, etc.) — see source guide section 4.
8. **Pro bono** — [[Advocate]], [[LawWorks]] clinics, law school clinics — usually when cannot pay and legal aid unavailable.

### Legal aid (England & Wales)

Operated by the **Legal Aid Agency**. Eligibility depends on **means**, **scope**, and **merits** (with exceptions).

**Find a legal aid provider:** [find-legal-advice.justice.gov.uk](https://www.find-legal-advice.justice.gov.uk)

**Public eligibility check:** [gov.uk/check-legal-aid](https://www.gov.uk/check-legal-aid)

**Civil Legal Advice (phone, if eligible):** 0345 345 4 345 — [gov.uk/civil-legal-advice](https://www.gov.uk/civil-legal-advice)

#### Criminal legal aid

- Free advice at **police interview under caution** (not means-tested).
- Magistrates’ court: “interests of justice” test + means (gross income threshold **£22,325** cited in guide).
- Crown Court: interests of justice test passed automatically; disposable income threshold **£37,500** cited in guide.
- Guidance: [gov.uk/guidance/criminal-legal-aid-means-testing](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/criminal-legal-aid-means-testing)

#### Civil legal aid — simplified means (guide summary; check current rules)

- Gross income ≤ **£2,657/month** and disposable income ≤ **£733/month** (certain benefits may “passport” the income test).
- Capital ≤ **£8,000** disposable assets (**£3,000** for immigration). Home equity counted but **£100,000** equity disregarded in the means test.
- Contributions may be required even when eligible.
- Means test disapplied in some proceedings (e.g. some care proceedings, Mental Health Tribunal, Hague Convention cases).

#### Civil issues often **in scope** (verify at source)

Homelessness/loss of home or serious disrepair; urgent protection from abuse; discrimination; asylum; some immigration (trafficking, domestic abuse victims, separated migrant children, bail); benefits appeals on points of law; mental health detention challenges; some family matters involving domestic abuse or child risk; coroner’s inquest where family member died; challenging certain government decisions.

#### Often **out of scope**

Most consumer/contract disputes; most private family (unless domestic abuse/child abuse risk); most immigration; personal injury; wills/trusts/conveyancing; defamation (with exceptions).

**Exceptional Case Funding** where human rights would be breached without legal aid: [gov.uk/guidance/legal-aid-apply-for-exceptional-case-funding](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/legal-aid-apply-for-exceptional-case-funding)

**Domestic abuse:** legal aid may cover private family matters with evidence of abuse; eligibility waiver for urgent protective orders; up to **£100,000** home equity disregarded if victim left home; support for migrant victims applying for independent settlement.

### National advice networks

| Service | Role | Contact / link |
|---------|------|----------------|
| **Advicelocal** | Postcode-based local advice finder | [advicelocal.uk](https://advicelocal.uk) |
| **Citizens Advice** | General and specialist advice | [citizensadvice.org.uk](https://www.citizensadvice.org.uk) |
| **Law Centres** | Charity law practices, social welfare law | [lawcentres.org.uk](https://lawcentres.org.uk) |
| **AdviceUK** | Network of advice organisations | [adviceuk.org.uk](https://www.adviceuk.org.uk) |
| **LawWorks Clinics** | ~300 free initial advice clinics | [lawworks.org.uk/clinics](https://www.lawworks.org.uk/clinics) |
| **Support Through Court** | Non-legal support for litigants in person | [supportthroughcourt.org](https://www.supportthroughcourt.org) |

### Pro bono (England & Wales)

**[[Advocate]]** — barrister pro bono; England & Wales; all areas of law; apply at [weareadvocate.org.uk](https://www.weareadvocate.org.uk); enquiries@weareadvocate.org.uk; 020 4518 6141 (voicemail). Hearing/deadline usually **more than 3 weeks** after completed application.

**[[LawWorks]]** — solicitor pro bono; clinic network, [freelegalanswers.org.uk](https://www.freelegalanswers.org.uk), charity advice programme.

### Cost of living

National signposting includes [gov.uk/cost-of-living](https://www.gov.uk/cost-of-living), Citizens Advice cost-of-living pages, Money Helper, National Debtline, local council Household Support Fund, Help through Hardship line **0808 208 2138** (Citizens Advice / Trussell Trust).

## Practical Guidance

1. Start with [[Signposting to Free Legal Advice]] principles.
2. Run [gov.uk/check-legal-aid](https://www.gov.uk/check-legal-aid) for civil issues.
3. For eviction/repossession risk, use [[Housing Loss Prevention Advice Service]] immediately — not means-tested.
4. Locate local help on [advicelocal.uk](https://advicelocal.uk).
5. If client is in **Wales** with housing, education, or health/social care issues, switch to [[Free Legal Advice in Wales]].
6. For barrister representation when legal aid refused/unavailable: [[Advocate]].
7. Consult the full PDF for **issue-specific charities** (section 4: employment, immigration, domestic abuse, etc.).

## Related Concepts

- [[Courts and Disputes]]
- [[Legal aid]]
- [[Pro Bono and Free Legal Advice]]
- [[Signposting to Free Legal Advice]]
- [[Housing Loss Prevention Advice Service]]
- [[Free Legal Advice in Wales]]

## Related Organisations

- [[Attorney General Pro Bono Committee]]
- [[Advocate]]
- [[LawWorks]]
- [[Citizens Advice]]
- [[Advicenow]]

## Sources

- **Attorney General’s Pro Bono Committee** — *Guide to Pro Bono and Other Free Advice in England & Wales* (November 2025) — [probonocommittee.uk/guide](https://probonocommittee.uk/guide) — `raw/bar-council/Guide_to_Pro_Bono_and_Other_Free_Advice_in_England__Wales_November_2025.pdf`

# Free Legal Advice in Scotland

## Summary

The November 2024 **Guide to Pro Bono and Other Free Advice in Scotland** signposts legal aid (via the Scottish Legal Aid Board), Citizens Advice Scotland, Scottish law centres, pro bono (including the Faculty of Advocates Free Legal Services Unit), and specialist charities. **Scots law differs materially from England & Wales** — prefer Scottish organisations and resources.

## Key Information

### Devolved law warning

Resources written for England & Wales may be unsuitable. Signpost to Scottish bodies or UK-wide charities with Scottish arms (e.g. Age Scotland). State that the matter is based in Scotland when referring.

### Overview of help sources

1. **Online** — [advicelocal.uk](https://advicelocal.uk) (Scots law sections), [advicenow.org.uk](https://advicenow.org.uk), Citizens Advice Scotland.
2. **Insurance / trade union** — as in other jurisdictions.
3. **Private lawyers** — [lawscot.org.uk/find-a-solicitor](https://www.lawscot.org.uk/find-a-solicitor); advocates normally instructed via solicitor: [advocates.org.uk/instructing-advocates](https://www.advocates.org.uk/instructing-advocates).
4. **Legal aid** — Scottish Legal Aid Board (SLAB); see below.
5. **Local advice** — Citizens Advice bureaux, law centres; [cas.org.uk/bureaux](https://www.cas.org.uk/bureaux), [mygov.scot/legal-advice](https://www.mygov.scot/legal-advice).
6. **Specialist charities** — issue-specific (see source guide).
7. **Pro bono** — FLSU, LawWorks Scotland clinics, university clinics.

### Legal aid (Scotland)

**Information:** [mygov.scot/legal-aid](https://www.mygov.scot/legal-aid), [slab.org.uk](https://www.slab.org.uk)

**Eligibility estimators:** [slab.org.uk/new-to-legal-aid/eligibility-estimators](https://www.slab.org.uk/new-to-legal-aid/eligibility-estimators)

**Find a solicitor:** [lawscot.org.uk/find-a-solicitor](https://www.lawscot.org.uk/find-a-solicitor) (legal aid filter) or [slab.org.uk/new-to-legal-aid/find-a-solicitor](https://www.slab.org.uk/new-to-legal-aid/find-a-solicitor)

Eligibility depends on **scope**, **means**, and **merits** (with limited exceptions). Many people are not eligible even when they cannot afford private lawyers; providers may be unavailable.

#### Criminal legal aid

- Most criminal cases in scope except minor offences.
- Free advice at police station (not means-tested).
- Courts: interests of justice + means — [mygov.scot/legal-aid/criminal-cases](https://www.mygov.scot/legal-aid/criminal-cases)
- **Public Defence Solicitors’ Office:** [pdso.org.uk](https://www.pdso.org.uk)

#### Civil legal aid

- **Civil Legal Assistance Office (CLAO):** [clao.org.uk](https://www.clao.org.uk) — advice centres for certain areas/parts of country.
- Civil means test: online estimator at SLAB; many financially ineligible.
- **Often in scope (verify):** benefits, children’s hearings, money claims, criminal injury, debt, discrimination, divorce/separation, domestic abuse, employment, housing, immigration/asylum (listed types), mental health, some personal injury, police trouble.
- **Often out of scope:** most consumer/contract disputes; most private family (unless domestic abuse/violence/child abuse); most immigration; personal injury/death; conveyancing; wills/trusts; business law; defamation (with defender exceptions).

### National advice networks

| Service | Contact / link |
|---------|----------------|
| **Citizens Advice Scotland** | 0800 028 1456; [citizensadvice.org.uk/scotland](https://www.citizensadvice.org.uk/scotland); bureaux: [cas.org.uk/bureaux](https://www.cas.org.uk/bureaux) |
| **Advicelocal** | [advicelocal.uk](https://advicelocal.uk) |
| **AdviceUK / AdviceFinder** | [advicefinder.turn2us.org.uk](https://advicefinder.turn2us.org.uk) |

### Scottish law centres (guide list)

**National:** Environmental Rights Centre for Scotland ([ercs.scot](https://ercs.scot)); Ethnic Minorities Law Centre ([emlc.org.uk](https://www.emlc.org.uk)); Clan Childlaw ([clanchildlaw.org](https://clanchildlaw.org)); JustRight Scotland ([justrightscotland.org.uk](https://justrightscotland.org.uk)); Legal Services Agency ([lsa.org.uk](https://www.lsa.org.uk)); Scottish Child Law Centre ([sclc.org.uk](https://www.sclc.org.uk)); Scottish Women’s Rights Centre ([scottishwomensrightscentre.org.uk](https://www.scottishwomensrightscentre.org.uk)); Shelter Scotland Housing Law Service ([scotland.shelter.org.uk](https://scotland.shelter.org.uk)).

**Regional/local examples:** Castlemilk Law and Money Advice Centre (Glasgow); Dundee Law Centre; Fife Law Centre; Govan Law Centre.

Most Scottish law centres are also legal aid providers.

### Pro bono — Faculty of Advocates FLSU

Scotland’s bar pro bono charity. Volunteer **devils** (trainee advocates) and **Members of Faculty** (advocates) provide:

- Court/tribunal representation
- Advice (meeting, phone, writing)
- Document drafting (e.g. skeleton arguments)

**Criteria (summary from guide):**

- Case based in **Scotland**
- Accredited agency instructed on applicant’s behalf
- Hearing/deadline **more than 3 weeks** after completed application (exceptions possible)
- Cannot afford to pay; cannot get legal aid

**Apply via accredited agency** — list at [advocates.org.uk](https://www.advocates.org.uk/instructing-advocates/free-legal-services-unit)

Contact: flsu@advocates.org.uk; **0131 226 5071**

Assistance **cannot be guaranteed**.

### Other Scotland pro bono (guide mentions)

- FLSU accredited advice agencies
- KIND UK — undocumented children immigration/nationality
- Ukraine Advice Project UK
- Scottish Women’s Rights Centre — women 16+ affected by violence/abuse

### LawWorks Scotland clinics

[lawworks.org.uk/catchment/all-scotland](https://www.lawworks.org.uk/catchment/all-scotland) — includes Edinburgh and Strathclyde university clinics.

### University law clinics (examples)

Aberdeen, Dundee, Edinburgh Napier, Edinburgh, Glasgow Caledonian, Robert Gordon, Strathclyde — see source guide for URLs.

### Cost of living (Scotland)

[mygov.scot/support-money-debt](https://www.mygov.scot/support-money-debt); [moneyadvicescotland.org.uk](https://www.moneyadvicescotland.org.uk); UK-wide: [gov.uk/cost-of-living](https://www.gov.uk/cost-of-living), National Debtline.

## Practical Guidance

1. Apply [[Signposting to Free Legal Advice]] — manage capacity expectations.
2. Use **SLAB estimators** before signposting to private or pro bono help.
3. Start with **Citizens Advice Scotland** or a **local law centre** for triage.
4. For advocate (barrister-equivalent) pro bono: referral through **FLSU accredited agency**, not direct public application.
5. Do **not** rely on England & Wales-only guides for substantive Scots law.
6. Locate foodbanks: [advicefinder.turn2us.org.uk](https://advicefinder.turn2us.org.uk).

# Free Legal Advice in Wales

## Summary

The **Wales guide** (Pro Bono Committee for Wales, November 2024) supplements the main England & Wales directory. It focuses on **devolved law** and **Welsh providers**. Legal aid rules are **the same as England** (not devolved). For UK-wide legal aid, pro bono, and issue-specific charities, use [[Free Legal Advice in England and Wales]] alongside this page.

Welsh-language version: [probonocommittee.uk/guide](https://probonocommittee.uk/guide)

## Key Information

### Signposting principles for Wales

- **Devolved areas:** housing, education, health & social care — prefer **Welsh organisations** familiar with Senedd legislation.
- **Legal aid:** not devolved; same rules as England ([[Free Legal Advice in England and Wales]]).
- **English charities** may serve Wales remotely but may lack Welsh legal expertise — state the client is in Wales when referring.
- **Extra factors:** services concentrate around Cardiff, Swansea, Wrexham; rural travel and digital exclusion; **Welsh language** rights — check Welsh-medium provision.
- **Capacity limits** apply as in the main guide.

### Devolved law — housing

Renting Homes (Wales) Act 2016 creates different landlord/tenant obligations than England. Limited housing advice capacity in Wales.

| Provider | Services | Contact |
|----------|----------|---------|
| **AdviceLink Cymru** (Citizens Advice Cymru / Welsh Government funded) | Housing, benefits, debt, employment, education, immigration, discrimination | 0800 702 2020 (9am–5pm Mon–Fri); private rent arrears: 0808 278 7920 |
| **Shelter Cymru** | Housing information, 23 local surgeries | 08000 495 495; [sheltercymru.org.uk](https://sheltercymru.org.uk) |
| **Gypsies and Travellers Wales** | Accommodation, homelessness, benefits, planning | 029 2021 4411 |
| **Travelling Ahead** (TGP Cymru) | Gypsy, Roma, Traveller accommodation advocacy | 0808 802 0025 |
| **The Wallich** | Homelessness charity; legal advice for service users via Cardiff Lawyers Care | 029 2066 8464 |
| **Public Services Ombudsman for Wales** | Complaints about social landlords | 0300 790 0203 |

Homelessness support: [gov.wales/support-if-you-are-homeless-or-about-become-homeless](https://www.gov.wales/support-if-you-are-homeless-or-about-become-homeless)

### Devolved law — education

Welsh curriculum, ALN system (replacing SEN), student finance, and school obligations differ from England.

| Provider | Focus | Contact |
|----------|-------|---------|
| **SNAP Cymru** | ALN/SEN, exclusions, discrimination, advocacy | 0808 801 0608 |
| **TGP Cymru** | Children, education, statutory advocacy regions | 029 2039 6974 |
| **NYAS Cymru** | Care-experienced children and young people | 0808 808 1001 |
| **Children’s Legal Centre Wales** | Online resources | [childrenslegalcentre.wales](https://childrenslegalcentre.wales) |

### Devolved law — health & social care

NHS Wales structure (7 local health boards, 3 trusts); **Putting Things Right** redress scheme (legal advice for claims ≤£25,000 via accredited solicitors); distinct social care framework.

| Provider | Focus | Contact |
|----------|-------|---------|
| **Advocacy Support Cymru** | Healthcare advocacy (various UHB areas) | 029 2054 0444 |
| **Age Cymru** | Over-50s advice (direct contact only) | 0300 303 44 98 |
| **Mencap Cymru** | Learning disability healthcare rights | 0808 8000 300 |
| **Mind Cymru** | Mental health rights; Legal Line | 0300 466 6463 |
| **Tenovus** | Cancer — benefits advice, free wills in Wales | 0808 808 1010 |

### Pro bono clinics (examples)

Search current clinics: [lawworks.org.uk/clinics](https://www.lawworks.org.uk/clinics); Wales contact: lawworkscymru@lawworks.org.uk

Examples listed in guide: Aberystwyth Family Law Clinic; ACE Cardiff children law clinic; Bangor, Cardiff, Swansea university clinics; LGBTQ+ Law Clinic; Cardiff Innocence Project; Redkite at the Table (Carmarthen); USW Legal Advice Clinic; Veterans Legal Link (UK-wide).

### General Wales advice organisations (selected)

| Organisation | Areas | Contact |
|--------------|-------|---------|
| **Asylum Justice** | Immigration/asylum to OISC Level 3 | 029 2049 9421 |
| **Advocate** | Barrister pro bono (all areas) | 020 4518 6141 |
| **Speakeasy Law Centre** | Only law centre in Wales; benefits, debt, housing; employment clinic (South Wales) | 029 2045 3111 |
| **North Wales Community Law** | Housing (domestic abuse intersection) | 01492 484818 |
| **Riverside Advice** | Benefits, housing, debt, energy (Cardiff-based, Wales-wide) | 029 2034 1577 |
| **Settled** | EUSS / late applications (Newport HQ) | 0330 223 5336 |
| **Welsh Refugee Council** | Sanctuary seekers — housing, benefits, legal advice | 0808 196 7273 |
| **Welsh Women’s Aid** | Domestic abuse | Live Fear Free **0808 80 10 800** (24h) |
| **Planning Aid Wales** | Planning law helpline | 029 2062 5000 |
| **Qualia Law CIC** | Court of Protection, mental capacity | 0333 305 3057 |

### Citizens Advice Cymru

National Advicelink: **0800 702 2020**. Additional helplines include Consumer (0808 223 1133), Help to Claim UC (08000 241 220), private rented debt (0808 278 7920). Local bureaux listed by county in source guide — find via [citizensadvice.org.uk/wales](https://www.citizensadvice.org.uk/wales).

### Wales online directories

- [dewis.wales](https://dewis.wales) — wellbeing services
- [en.infoengine.cymru](https://en.infoengine.cymru) — third sector directory
- [ombudsman.wales/advice-advocates](https://www.ombudsman.wales/advice-advocates)
- [gov.wales/help-cost-living](https://www.gov.wales/help-cost-living)
- [law.gov.wales](https://law.gov.wales) — devolved law information

## Practical Guidance

1. Confirm the issue is in a **devolved** area (housing, education, health/social care) — if yes, start with Welsh providers above.
2. For **legal aid**, use the same routes as England ([find-legal-advice.justice.gov.uk](https://www.find-legal-advice.justice.gov.uk)).
3. For **eviction/repossession**, use [[Housing Loss Prevention Advice Service]] (applies in Wales; housing **law** is still devolved for substance of dispute).
4. Mention **Welsh language** preference when referring.
5. Cross-check issue-specific charities in the England & Wales guide if no Welsh equivalent exists.

- [[Housing Loss Prevention Advice Service]]

- [[Advocate]]
- [[LawWorks]]

# Advocate

## Summary

**Advocate** is the Bar of England and Wales’ pro bono charity. It matches people who need court advice or representation with volunteer **barristers** when they cannot afford to pay and **legal aid is unavailable**.

## Key Information

| Field | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Geographical remit** | England and Wales (including clients in Wales) |
| **Areas of law** | All areas |
| **Help provided** | Representation in court/tribunal; advice (meeting, phone, writing); drafting (e.g. skeleton arguments) |
| **In person** | No — remote/online processing |
| **Pro bono** | Yes — all volunteer barristers |

### Eligibility (summary — verify at source)

- Need a barrister for the case
- Case based in England and Wales
- Hearing or deadline **more than 3 weeks** after a **completed** application (exceptions possible)
- Cannot pay; legal aid unavailable

### Application

- **Direct application** by the public is allowed (no referral required).
- Agencies or MPs can help collate documents and write a concise summary.
- Online application; paper forms available by phone/post for those without web access.

### Contact

- Website: [weareadvocate.org.uk](https://www.weareadvocate.org.uk)
- Email: enquiries@weareadvocate.org.uk
- Phone: 020 4518 6141 (**voicemail only**)

**Assistance cannot be guaranteed.**

## Practical Guidance

1. Check **legal aid** first ([gov.uk/check-legal-aid](https://www.gov.uk/check-legal-aid)).
2. Confirm the hearing is **at least 3 weeks away** (or ask Advocate about exceptions).
3. Apply via [weareadvocate.org.uk/how-our-service-works.html](https://www.weareadvocate.org.uk/how-our-service-works.html).
4. For clients in **Wales**, Advocate can still help — note Welsh devolved law context in the application.
5. Scotland uses the **Faculty of Advocates FLSU** instead — see [[Free Legal Advice in Scotland]].

## Related Concepts

- [[Courts and Disputes]]
- [[Legal aid]]
- [[Pro Bono and Free Legal Advice]]
- [[Free Legal Advice in England and Wales]]
- [[Signposting to Free Legal Advice]]

## Related Organisations

# Attorney General Pro Bono Committee

## Summary

The **Attorney General’s Pro Bono Committee of England & Wales** oversees the annual **Guide to Pro Bono and Other Free Advice** directories published for UK Pro Bono Week. The guides signpost parliamentarians, caseworkers, and the public to legal aid, pro bono, advice agencies, and specialist charities — they do not provide legal advice themselves.

## Key Information

### Publications

| Guide | Jurisdiction | Wiki |
|-------|--------------|------|
| Main directory | England & Wales | [[Free Legal Advice in England and Wales]] |
| Wales supplement | Devolved Welsh law & providers | [[Free Legal Advice in Wales]] |
| Scotland directory | Scots law & providers | [[Free Legal Advice in Scotland]] |

**Download hub:** [probonocommittee.uk/guide](https://probonocommittee.uk/guide)

**Wales committee:** [wales.probonocommittee.uk](https://wales.probonocommittee.uk)

### Pro Bono Week

Cross-sector initiative each November promoting voluntary free legal help. Guides are updated annually; details may go out of date — check organisation websites.

### Feedback

Corrections and additions: **guide@probonocommittee.uk**

### Disclaimer (from guides)

- Guides do not provide legal or financial advice.
- Listings are not guaranteed comprehensive; no warranty on organisations’ capacity, quality, or suitability.
- Verify opening hours and services on provider websites.

## Practical Guidance

1. Use [[Pro Bono and Free Legal Advice]] as the wiki entry point.
2. Follow [[Signposting to Free Legal Advice]] when referring clients.
3. Download the latest PDF from [probonocommittee.uk/guide](https://probonocommittee.uk/guide) for full issue-specific charity listings.
4. Report errors to guide@probonocommittee.uk.

## Related Concepts

- [[Courts and Disputes]]
- [[Legal aid]]
- [[Pro Bono and Free Legal Advice]]
- [[Signposting to Free Legal Advice]]

## Related Organisations

- [[Advocate]]
- [[LawWorks]]
- [[Citizens Advice]]

# LawWorks

## Summary

**LawWorks** (operating name of the Solicitors Pro Bono Group) connects people and not-for-profit organisations with **volunteer solicitors** for free legal help. It runs the national **LawWorks Clinics Network** (~300 clinics), **Free Legal Answers** online advice, and programmes for small charities.

## Key Information

### LawWorks Clinics Network

- Around **300 clinics** offering free **initial** legal advice (typically 30–60 minutes).
- Areas include employment, housing, consumer, debt, welfare rights, family, immigration (varies by clinic).
- Geographic, demographic, and subject limits apply per clinic.
- Student-run clinics may have reduced availability in holidays/exam periods.
- Find clinics: [lawworks.org.uk/clinics](https://www.lawworks.org.uk/clinics) (search by postcode and area of law).
- **Wales:** lawworkscymru@lawworks.org.uk

### Free Legal Answers

- Online platform for low-income users to ask civil law questions.
- Eligibility questions on signup.
- [freelegalanswers.org.uk](https://www.freelegalanswers.org.uk)

### Not-for-profits programme

Legal advice brokered to small charities: [lawworks.org.uk/legal-advice-not-profits](https://www.lawworks.org.uk/legal-advice-not-profits)

### Secondary specialisation projects

In-depth supervised pro bono in areas such as unpaid wages and community care for families of children with life-limiting conditions.

## Practical Guidance

1. Search [lawworks.org.uk/clinics](https://www.lawworks.org.uk/clinics) for local clinic scope and contact details.
2. Use **Free Legal Answers** for short written civil queries if eligible.
3. Clinics give **initial** advice — not full representation in every case.
4. Check legal aid before pro bono routes — see [[Free Legal Advice in England and Wales]].
5. Scotland clinics: [lawworks.org.uk/catchment/all-scotland](https://www.lawworks.org.uk/catchment/all-scotland).

## Related Concepts

- [[Courts and Disputes]]
- [[Legal aid]]
- [[Pro Bono and Free Legal Advice]]
- [[Free Legal Advice in England and Wales]]
- [[Free Legal Advice in Wales]]
